doc.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Piano and horn influences
summary: Tatum, Teddy Wilson, Bud Powell and Charlie Parker shaped his style.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Who are some of the first — you mentioned Avery Parrish of course and Erskine Hawkins. Were there other people that caught your ear as a young man, that directed you to jazz?

Who were my main influences, I mean pianistically as far as I’m concerned, well I should say who did I listen to, who did I really like listening to was, number one would be Art Tatum. And Teddy Wilson. And then with the advent of the bebop era of course Bud Powell. And I think maybe a couple of horn players influenced my style too, like the linear things that I do, I think about Charlie Parker, with whom I had the great honor and privilege of playing with a couple of times. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
